content.intro: Use this lesson on accessibility fundamentals for jquery interfaces as a professional review habit: identify the relevant behavior, make one controlled change, and verify its outcome.
content.why_it_matters: This topic is useful because it turns semantic html into a repeatable implementation choice. Accessible interactions use semantic elements, keyboard controls, visible focus, meaningful status updates, and synchronized ARIA state. Secure interfaces render untrusted data safely and rely on server controls for sensitive actions.

common_mistakes: Assuming a selector matched an element without checking the collection length.
Confusing jQuery collections with native DOM elements or live properties with markup attributes.
Using .html() with untrusted data or assuming client-side validation enforces server rules.
Treating a demo snippet as production-ready without testing failure and accessibility states.
